Rome —
They are two of the world’s best-known Bobs from the US Midwest. Now Pope Leo XIV, whose birth name is Robert Prevost, and Bob Dylan, the legendary musician, have met in the Vatican.
Leo and Dylan were both seen meeting in the Vatican’s apostolic palace, the pope’s residence, on Wednesday. The pope was wearing his white cassock and Dylan a black coat, black gloves and a black hoodie.
The meeting was brokered by Rev. Antonio Spadaro, a Vatican official known for building bridges between the church and wider culture. Spadaro earlier this year arranged a meeting between Pope Leo and Patti Smith.
“It was hard not to feel the emotion of being part of an encounter that had a real sense of history about it, with the feeling that, at every step through the Apostolic Palace, absolutely anything could happen!” Spadaro wrote on social media platforms...

At least seven flights and a cruise ship in Europe received bomb threats on Tuesday, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered.
At least two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to ​Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday, and another flight to ‌Sofia had been threatened a day earlier. An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.
There was no claim of responsibility and officials did not attribute blame. None of the affected airlines responded to Reuters’ requests for comment.

In Europe this summer, it was a sight almost as ubiquitous as the sun: fashionistas weaving their way down Mediterranean beach promenades, London high streets and haute couture centers in Paris carrying earthy-colored, basket or crochet-patterned bags.
The rise of raffia bags was first ignited by 1960s fashion trendsetters like Brigitte Bardot and Jacqueline Kennedy. Once a casual holiday accessory, raffia totes and clutches have blossomed into mass-market must-haves and cornerstone items for luxury fashion houses; Prada, Saint Laurent and Loewe represent just a few of the designer brands to curate raffia products that retail with four-figure price tags.
